architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept consistency with the E1-derived H-CORE benchmark if the mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent preparations is between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive, corresponding to 9.51% plus or minus the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If mean SI_15_60 is below 7.51%, falsify transfer of H-CORE's 9.51% prediction to S1C02 because the downward deviation exceeds 2.00 percentage points. A mean above 11.51% rejects agreement with the benchmark but does not satisfy the registry's directional falsification rule for H-CORE; it indicates additional core-composition or process dependence. No outcome from this modifier-free candidate can falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run M-HOLD-120 on a catalogued E2-core acrylic-only candidate with nonzero acrylic-like modifier and zero minor tackifier-like modifier, using the same recorded preparation history and at least two independent preparations; compare its mean SI_15_60 with 9.51% multiplied by its reactive mass fraction and with half of that linear benchmark.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured at 120 C; individual-repeat values are also retained.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 is scientifically defensible as a replicated baseline probe of whether the E1-derived 9.51% core benchmark transfers to the central E2 reactive core. It cannot adjudicate H-RESIN or H-DUAL, so no resin- or tackifier-specific claim is attached to its outcome. The direct hold measurement is preferable to temperature-sweep or state-anchor measurements for the declared thermal-hold failure mode.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Proposer's selection of S1C02::M-HOLD-120 because it is a supplied, operationally selectable card that directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate, but I follow the Skeptic in restricting its interpretation to H-CORE benchmark transfer and correcting the threshold to the registered 7.51% resolution boundary. I do not follow the Robustness Adjudicator's preferred acrylic-only experiment because UNASSIGNED_ACRYLIC_ONLY_E2 is not a supplied candidate card and cannot be selected without inventing an operational identity. The tied core-only cards are broken in favor of S1C02 because it is the measured central E2 anchor with directly documented realization-state risk.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Only single original hold trajectories exist for E1 and E5, and S1C02 has no prior hold trajectory. Because S1C02 activates neither modifier axis, this card provides no evidence about resin suppression or tackifier necessity.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for temperature and time because the experiment stays at 120 C and within 15-60 min. Formulation-transfer uncertainty remains because the 9.51% benchmark comes from E1, whereas S1C02 is the E2 core with different NCO:OH and MDI fraction.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 directly reads SI_15_60 without regression or extrapolation and has a declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination threshold. At least two independent preparations are required, with the arithmetic mean preregistered as the decision statistic.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Substantial: E2 showed a 3.57-fold max/min viscosity spread at 120 C, M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state, and six process fields are missing. Preparation history must therefore be controlled and recorded, and eta_15 plus individual-repeat drift values retained.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C, with large formulation-dependent thermal-hold drift.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 hold increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min and by 93.08% from 15 to 90 min at 120 C, whereas E1 increased by 9.51% and 16.85% over the same respective windows.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local isothermal-hold data, each represented by one four-point run at 120 C. There are no independent hold repeats and no hold trajectory for the E2 reactive-core anchor or for resin-axis candidates. By contrast, temperature response is measured over 80-130 C in multiple runs, and realized viscosity-level variability is at least directly characterized for E2 by three-run spreads at six temperatures.
measurement_requirements: Use the matched-window 120 C hold protocol: measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15.
Run at least two independent preparations so the drift comparison is not based on a single realization.
Use a composition with nonzero acrylic-like modifier and zero minor tackifier-like modifier if the goal is to distinguish H-RESIN from the tackifier-required H-DUAL prediction.

Calculate the preregistered H-CORE benchmark as E1 drift multiplied by the candidate reactive mass fraction, and compare the measured drift both with that benchmark and with the H-RESIN threshold of less than half the linear-dilution prediction.
Apply the declared 2 percentage-point matched-window discrimination resolution and freeze all decision thresholds before observing the result.
Record and control preparation and process history, and retain the realized viscosity at 15 min, because E2 temperature-sweep realizations show approximately 2.80-3.57-fold max/min spread.
Keep inference within the measured 120 C and 15-60 min window, preserve the source viscosity unit as unknown, and do not infer a molecular reaction pathway from rheology alone.
planner.scientific_question: For an acrylic-only resin-modified composition with known reactive mass fraction, does the replicated 15-to-60 min viscosity drift at 120 C remain consistent with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, or fall substantially below it as predicted by H-RESIN? In particular, low drift without a minor tackifier would also falsify the tackifier-required prediction of H-DUAL.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 4.75% across at least two preparations would falsify the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for this reactive-core anchor by more than the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. Because S1C02 contains neither acrylic-like modifier nor minor tackifier, this outcome would not establish H-RESIN and would not test H-DUAL; it would instead show that the E1-derived core benchmark is not transferable to E2 under the controlled protocol.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: Drift at or near 9.51% would support transfer of the H-CORE benchmark to E2 within measurement resolution. A value materially above 9.51% would show additional core-composition or process dependence rather than simple benchmark transfer. In either case, H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain untested because no modifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 4.75% and 9.51% would indicate partial suppression relative to the benchmark but would satisfy neither the preregistered H-RESIN threshold nor a clean H-CORE comparison unless it lies within 2 percentage points of 9.51%. It would motivate a controlled acrylic-only hold experiment, but would not adjudicate resin or tackifier necessity.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly during a replicated 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is the already characterized E1 reactive-core composition used to define the 9.51% reference, so replication is useful but provides less novelty than measuring the unobserved E2 hold trajectory.
It is a measured reactive-core composition, but it is a stoichiometric perturbation away from the registered E2 anchor and lacks E2's explicit repeatability-risk characterization.
It measures drift directly but uses an interpolated rather than measured reactive-core composition, adding unnecessary composition uncertainty while still separating no registered hypotheses.
It directly addresses realization-state spread and lowers process-state risk, but it does not observe the thermal-hold drift coordinate on which H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL disagree.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared failure mode in the supported 120 C, 15-60 min window and avoids regression or shared-shape model assumptions. S1C02 is the strongest choice within the reported top tie because it is the measured central E2 anchor and its large 120 C realization spread makes independent preparations essential. However, all supplied top-tied cards are reactive-core-only and have identical registered predictions, so this experiment separates none of H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL. The planner's decisive acrylic-only intervention would be scientifically superior for pairwise hypothesis discrimination, but no acrylic-only candidate ID is present among the supplied experiment cards.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All nine tied cards have the same VOI component vector and separate no registered hypothesis pairs. S1C02 is preferred because it is the measured E2 reactive-core anchor at the geometric center of the original local design, has direct 80-130 C support, and is the only tied composition for which substantial realization-state variability was explicitly quantified. Replicated hold measurements therefore provide the cleanest new baseline for the least-resolved isothermal-time coordinate without introducing an interpolated core composition.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the standalone reactive-core-only S1C02 intervention with an E2-core acrylic-only formulation in the preregistered 15-20% initial band, with 0% minor tackifier, and run the matched-window 120 C hold alongside S1C02 as a process-matched control. This departure from the deterministic tied top set is justified by registered hypothesis discrimination that the score's minimality-first ordering failed to prioritize. The payload supplies no candidate ID for the required acrylic-only formulation.
residual_decision_risk: The required acrylic-only candidate has no supplied catalog ID or experiment card, so its exact formulation cannot be operationally selected from this payload.
The decision-stability report is withheld, preventing assessment of top-set stability, the margin to the first strictly lower experiment, and weight-specific flip boundaries.
Preparation-state variability is large for E2, while M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state; preparation history and repeat aggregation must be frozen before measurement.
The proposal does not specify whether thresholds apply to every repeat, the mean, or another preregistered aggregate.
The 4.75% superlinear-suppression threshold and the 2 percentage-point H-CORE resolution rule create a 4.75-7.51% region that requires explicit, preregistered interpretation.

An acrylic-only arm can distinguish H-RESIN from H-CORE and can falsify the tackifier-required H-DUAL prediction if low drift occurs, but complete separation across all three hypotheses is stronger with the proposed matched 2x2 modifier design.
Rheological drift can adjudicate formulation-level predictions but cannot establish a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The objection is design-changing, not merely interpretive. S1C02 activates neither modifier axis, gives H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL identical 9.51% predictions, and separates no hypothesis pair. It can establish an E2 hold baseline and test transfer of the E1-derived benchmark, but it cannot answer the stated acrylic-only scientific question or adjudicate resin suppression or tackifier necessity. A controlled acrylic-only formulation based on the E2 core, with 15-20% acrylic-like modifier and exactly 0% minor tackifier, measured by M-HOLD-120 alongside a matched unmodified E2 control, is scientifically preferable. No catalogued candidate ID for that formulation is supplied, so an exact existing candidate card cannot be selected without inventing an ID.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The decision-stability layer was withheld, so top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary are unavailable. Therefore no specific weight perturbation that changes the tied top set, or judgment about the scientific defensibility of such a weighting, can be established from the supplied payload. The visible deterministic score places S1C02::M-HOLD-120 in the nine-member tied top set, but that does not resolve the scientific inadequacy shared by that set.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol can numerically produce an SI_15_60 below 4.75% and thereby challenge transfer of the E1-derived H-CORE benchmark to E2. It cannot validly meet the full stated criterion: S1C02 is not acrylic-only or resin-modified, so no outcome can falsify H-DUAL through acrylic-only low drift or falsify H-RESIN at a resin-modified composition. The H-CORE cutoff is also inconsistent with the registered 2.00 percentage-point resolution rule because 4.75-7.51% is beyond resolution relative to 9.51% but is not classified as falsification.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that this experiment adjudicates resin-mediated suppression or tackifier necessity would be unsupported; it can only establish an E2 hold baseline and test transfer of the E1-derived H-CORE benchmark.
objections.objection: S1C02 has 0.0% AC1920 and 0.0% TK100, and the hypothesis_discrimination_detail assigns the same 9.51% prediction to H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL with separated_pairs = []. Therefore S1C02::M-HOLD-120 separates none of the three registered hypotheses. The Proposer correctly admits this in hypotheses_not_separated and hypotheses_separated, but the experiment card still incorrectly says that drift below 4.75% would accept H-RESIN over H-CORE.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low or high E2 drift could be misattributed to failure of linear dilution when it could instead reflect core-composition differences or uncontrolled preparation state; no modifier-specific effect can be inferred.
objections.objection: The 9.51% benchmark comes from E1, while the proposed formulation is E2. E1 has NCO:OH = 1.7 and 19.2867% MDI, whereas E2 has NCO:OH = 1.8 and 20.1907% MDI. Thus a difference from 9.51% changes reactive-core stoichiometry/composition as well as formulation identity. In addition, M-HOLD-120 is marked controls_process_state = false, with six missing process fields and process_state_risk = 0.75. Neither modifier axis moves at all, so acrylic suppression, tackifier suppression, and acrylic-versus-tackifier specialization are unavailable as mechanism attributions.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The drift values remain directly interpretable, but borderline or discordant repeats could be adjudicated post hoc despite the prohibition on post-result adjudication.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60, with no regression, extrapolation, or imputation. However, the decision phrase "across at least two repeats" does not specify whether every repeat must cross the threshold, whether the mean is used, or how disagreement between repeats is handled.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Results could be labeled as falsifying H-RESIN or H-DUAL when those hypotheses were never instantiated, and measurable H-CORE deviations between 4.75% and 7.51% could be incorrectly denied falsification status.
objections.objection: The experiment-card falsification criterion is not valid as written. It says H-DUAL is falsified if "this acrylic-only composition" reaches low drift, but S1C02 contains 0.0% acrylic and is reactive-core-only. It also says H-RESIN is falsified at or above 9.51%, although H-RESIN is defined for a resin-modified composition and no resin axis is active here. Only the H-CORE numerical branch is operationally attainable: the protocol could measure drift below 4.75%. Even that threshold is stricter than the registered H-CORE rule: with a 9.51% prediction and 2.00 percentage-point resolution, values below 7.51% are already beyond resolution, whereas the proposal labels 4.75-7.51% as intermediate.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: There is no identified outcome leakage, but any later claim that the hold result proves a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism would exceed the measurement's scope.
objections.objection: No target-validation identity, target hold result, or outcome-derived label is visibly used, and the Proposer appropriately limits inference to formulation-level rheology rather than a molecular reaction pathway. The molecular wording in H-RESIN about effective concentration and encounter frequency could not be established by this rheological hold alone, but the proposed core-only experiment explicitly says it would not establish H-RESIN.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the core-only S1C02 intervention with a controlled acrylic-only formulation based on the E2 core, using a nonzero acrylic-like fraction in the preregistered 15-20% initial band and exactly 0% minor tackifier, and run it alongside an unmodified E2 control prepared under the same recorded process history. Apply H-CORE using each formulation's reactive mass fraction and preregister repeat aggregation. To separate all three hypotheses rather than only H-RESIN from the H-CORE/H-DUAL pair, extend this to a matched 2x2 modifier design: no modifier, acrylic-only, tackifier-only, and acrylic-plus-tackifier, all with the same normalized E2 reactive core and matched process controls.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02 activates neither modifier axis, gives H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL the identical 9.51% prediction, and therefore cannot provide the registered hypothesis discrimination claimed by the experiment-card acceptance and falsification language.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This must be loaded first to establish the state-aware response structure, state-calibration implications, local temperature sensitivity, and E1/E5 hold contrast before any candidate or experiment ranking.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: Needed to recover the evidence-derived E2 reactive-core anchor, independent acrylic and tackifier axes, and historical claim boundary before judging candidate experiments.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.
